text: Visiting Spider Cottage today, it is impossible to imagine it as anything other than the beautiful two bedroomed fully restored home that it now is. Aptly named given its location in The Web, the heart of the village of Crosshaven. The current owners bought this home 10 years ago when it was in a condition that needed some TLC to say the least. They set about improving the property while keeping an eye to the true history of the building. Originating from circa 1850 the property set out its journey as part of the overall Hayes Estate and part of a row of homes that were old coastguard cottages. The original configuration would have included having to walk through each room to get to the next. With the renovation works carried out at the property, it now presents a 700 sq. ft. two bedroomed cosy home. During the renovations the property was completely rewired, replumbed and high levels of insulation were installed as part of the process. New pipework was laid so it is easy to make the mistake of thinking the property has underfloor heating. Heating is actually by means of oil fired coupled with a wood burning stove so the home retains the heat really well. As part of the renovations all walls were stripped back inside and out and with the guidance of the people at Roundtower lime the proper limed mortar was used to reinstate. Heritage sash windows and complimenting front door were ordered and beneath a new roof cast iron gutters with the correct spikes were sourced to make sure the entire property read just as it did back in its heyday. To improve the internal accommodation a hallway to access bedrooms and bathroom was created. Some of the ceilings were raised and the extension to the rear of the property was enhanced to deliver a welcoming cosy bright room. The home now offers a beautiful lounge, an open plan kitchen cum dining room, two double bedrooms and a family bathroom. The choice of fittings used to finish the rooms was equally in keeping with the fabric of the building with bespoke fitted bookcases, display shelves and robes as well as some of the original doors repurposed for different rooms. The property has two independent attics to take care of storage needs and a third could be easily created should the need arise. The village lies at the mouth of the Owenabue River where it meets Cork Harbour offering breathtaking views of estuary, sea and maritime activity right from your doorstep. The village is steeped in seafaring history and charm, with scenic riverside walks, and a welcoming village centre with choice of cafes, pubs and local shops. It sits at the start of the hugely successful amenity walk and cycle path skirting the shoreline of the Owenabue estuary from Crosshaven to the adjoining satellite town of Carrigaline. Viewing of this home is a must to fully appreciate all that it has to offer. Arranged in an L shape the kitchen with a bright colour of ivory finish gives a host of cupboards at floor and eye level and allows for integrated appliances of fridge freezer, dishwasher and extractor over free standing cooker. A deep set Belfast sink sits within the solid oak counter top which received 8 coats of Danish oil on either side before being installed. Tiled between the extensive worktop space and overhead units. Fully glazed door leading to the back yard. The dining area is set against the backdrop of an exposed stone wall which would have been the original back wall of the cottage before its extension. This stone wall is accentuated and framed with bespoke cabinetry giving open shelves with panelled sides. A clever use of copper pipe gives a hanging rail for kitchen implements and is matched with the same theme open display shelving. The natural light in this room is tremendous from an extensive roof window fitted. A glazed door leads to the back which gives an element of storage. The entire room is finished in slate grey floor tile carried through with no thresholds from the rest of the reception rooms and accentuates the space. Living Room Rooms do not get much cosier than the living room at Spider Cottage. A deep set fireplace sits at its centre with a black cast iron stove fitted within the redbrick backdrop. The chimney was completely relined and a reclaimed heritage railway sleeper installed as the mantle. Bespoke units are fitted within the alcoves each side giving a host of storage, display selves and library effect. The entire room is painted in a calming jade green colour tone with a deeper shade used on the fitted furniture. Hallway Open to the living room a deep set arch leads through to the bedrooms. Finished with the same tiled floor to that in the reception space. Main bedroom A lovely double bedroom with built in bespoke headboard and side shelves. Early morning coffee in bed is a must to start leisurely days here taking in the waterside views. Wall to wall fitted robes are built in to take care of storage needs. The window has a lovely splay, finished with wood panelling and deep enough as a window seat with built in storage beneath. Finished with carpet and neutral tones in décor. Bedroom 2 Another lovely bedroom looking out over the front garden. This room has double robe fitted and finished with carpet. The deep set sash window allows for the creation of a natural window seat with storage beneath. Bathroom Located to the rear of the property is the family bathroom. Fitted with three piece white shower suite to include corner entry fully tiled shower cubicle complete with electric shower fitted. Finished with white brick style tiling the room is softened with painted wood panelling on the opposite wall. A dual function radiator and heated towel rail gives plenty of heat to this room. Wc and pedestal sink complete the suite. A Velux roof window takes care of natural light and joins with gable window for ventilation. Outside The front of the property has commanding water views enjoyed from a large lawned and partly enclosed garden to give privacy when needed. A newly laid patio to the front is directly adjacent to the home where al fresco dining is a must while taking in the vibrancy of the village and daily maritime activity. The rear of the property set against the backdrop of original wall of the Hayes estate gives an element of storage.
